result.title: Approximate Dynamic Programming with Basis Function Learning
result.summary: This work presents a novel approach for approximating the value function in Markov decision processes (MDPs). Our approach is grounded in the approximate linear programming (ALP) framework, wherein basis functions (BFs) play an important role. Traditionally, BFs have been pre-defined, randomly generated, or restricted to specific structures, which both limits the accuracy that can be achieved and leaves no mechanism for improving a given approximation. We instead learn BFs from the model itself, by repeatedly applying the Bellman operator to the current value estimate. We introduce the Bellman operator basis function (BOBF) learning method, and prove that each learned BF improves the approximation by a quantifiable amount and that the method converges to the optimal value function. Its shrunken counterpart (SBOBF) retains this guarantee while capping the number of BFs, and therefore the computational effort per iteration. For large-scale problems, where the number of constraints is prohibitive, we develop hybrid variants (HBOBF and SHBOBF) that combine constraint sampling with BF learning, and we show that the improvement and finite-termination guarantees are preserved under explicitly stated conditions. Numerical experiments on (continuous) perishable inventory and queueing control problems demonstrate that our BF learning techniques significantly outperform existing methods in the literature.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在近似线性规划框架下，通过反复对当前值估计施加 Bellman 算子从模型自身学习基函数（BOBF），证明每个新基函数带来可量化的逼近改进且方法收敛；并提出限制基函数数量的收缩版本及结合约束采样的混合变体，在易腐库存与排队控制问题上验证效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 「每新增一个基函数即带来量化改进、且可限制基函数总数」的机制，可能与 LVR 中潜推理状态如何逐步扩张、以及按计算预算决定何时停止更新形成概念类比，可供核查其状态表示与停止决策视角。
